title: Podcasts
summary: Spoken episodes written from Wikipedia or today's news and read aloud in the speech voices.
description: A podcast is listening practice on a subject the learner cares about. A writer model writes every sentence as a pair, Polish and English, from Wikipedia articles, from today's Polish news, or as a short made-up story. The speech model reads each line, and the clips are joined into one episode with pauses. An episode is stored as a song, so the player, playlists, casting and listening lessons all work on it.

requirements.text: An episode is written from 1 to 5 Wikipedia articles, from today's news, or from none as a made-up story.
An episode holds at most 120 sentences.
In the pairs format each sentence is said in English and then in Polish; in the immersion format only Polish is spoken and the English is shown with each line.
An episode can have a cast of up to 4 speakers, each keeping the same voice when the audio is made again.
The app can suggest subjects for an episode from what the learner is interested in.
A news episode is written from the headlines and summaries of Polish news feeds; the outlets' articles are only linked to.
The articles an episode was written from are kept as its sources and open in the app's reader.
Each sentence of an episode has its start and end time, so the player follows it like a song's lyrics.
Changing how an episode sounds (pauses, repeats, slow speech, English on or off) reuses the clips already made.
An episode's audio is stored as MP3.
